verdict.summary: Creating a V3 app is self-serve and works for your own account within the hour, but new apps are private: only the Constant Contact user who created the app can authorize it until you phone support (866-289-2101) to start an approval process with no published criteria or timeline. Plan around the per-API-key limit of 10,000 requests a day and 4 per second, which the docs state for the key rather than per connected account.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Sign up for a developer account (which creates a trial Constant Contact account), create the app, generate a secret, and authorize it with that same user.

timeToProd.assumes: An authorization-code app that reads and writes contacts and campaigns for any Constant Contact customer, which needs Constant Contact to lift the private-access restriction; there is no faster path for other users.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Constant Contact support's approval to open the app to all users, started by phone. A Technology Partner account (for managing client accounts) is a separate, several-week process.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The phone-call approval requirement is sourced; the docs give no duration, so the 1–3 week range is our estimate.

prerequisites.item: A V3 developer account (comes with a trial Constant Contact account)
prerequisites.why: My Applications is where you register apps and get the API key (client_id); signing up creates a trial account for testing.

prerequisites.item: Approval from Constant Contact to open the app to all users
prerequisites.why: New applications are limited to private access; only the creating user can grant access until support approves the app.

prerequisites.item: A redirect URI (absolute; wildcards only at domain root)
prerequisites.why: Authorization codes are returned to a registered redirect_uri. Multiple redirect URIs per app are allowed; the docs' examples use https://localhost:8888.

scopeTiers.impact: Read account details and get refresh tokens (offline_access). No scope is exempt from the private-access limit; approval is per app, not per scope.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: openid/profile/email are inferred from the documented id_token; the Scopes page lists only account_read, account_update, contact_data, campaign_data and offline_access.

scopeTiers.impact: Read and write contacts, lists, custom fields, segments, bulk activities and contact reports. What a CRM-sync or audience agent needs.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: reviewRequired=true reflects the app-level approval, not a scope-specific review.

scopeTiers.impact: Read and write email campaigns and read email reports. Lets an agent draft and schedule sends, so add your own confirmation step.
Create and manage Constant Contact client accounts under your partner account. Only for authorized technology partners; not needed to act on users' own accounts.

steps.title: Sign up for a developer account
steps.detail: In the V3 Developer Portal, open My Applications and click Sign up (email, password, name, organization, phone). A trial Constant Contact account is created for testing.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The portal URL returned HTTP 200 on 2026-10-20; we didn't sign in.

steps.title: Create the application
steps.detail: Click New Application, enter the consent-screen name, pick 'Authorization Code Flow and Implicit Flow' (server apps) or PKCE, and choose Rotating (recommended) or Long Lived refresh tokens. Developers are limited to 50 applications.

steps.title: Get the API key and generate a secret
steps.detail: Click edit on the app to see the API Key (client_id), click Generate Client Secret and store it; it's shown once. Add your redirect URIs and Save.

steps.title: Implement the authorization code flow
steps.detail: Redirect to https://authz.constantcontact.com/oauth2/default/v1/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, state and space-delimited scope (include offline_access). Exchange the code within 5 minutes at https://authz.constantcontact.com/oauth2/default/v1/token using Basic auth (base64 client_id:client_secret).

steps.title: Implement refresh handling
steps.detail: Refresh only when the access token is expired or close to it; each refresh returns a new refresh_token (store it atomically with rotating tokens). Refreshing before every call risks 429s on the token endpoint.

steps.title: Build a shared request budget
steps.detail: Track usage against 10,000 requests/day and 4 requests/second per API key, reset at 00:00 UTC. Back off on 429 with error_key 'throttled' and stop on 'quota_exceeded'. Use bulk activity endpoints for large imports.

steps.title: Test end to end with the creating user
steps.detail: Authorize the app with the same Constant Contact user that created it (the only user allowed before approval) and exercise each scope.

steps.title: Draft the approval request
steps.detail: Prepare a short description of the integration: app name and API key, scopes and why, expected number of connected accounts and daily request volume, and whether you'll need a higher rate limit.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Constant Contact doesn't publish what the approval asks for.

steps.title: Call support to open the app to all users
steps.detail: Call 866-289-2101 to begin the approval process that lets any Constant Contact user grant access.

steps.title: Wait for approval
steps.detail: No published SLA. Optionally apply as a Technology Partner in parallel if you need to provision client accounts; that review may take several weeks.

agentCanDo: Implement the authorization code or PKCE flow with offline_access
Handle rotating refresh tokens and token-endpoint backoff
Build a per-key daily and per-second request budget
Draft the approval request and scope justifications

Generate and store the client secret
Test authorization with the creating user

blockers.symptom: Other Constant Contact users can't authorize your app, while your own account works
blockers.cause: New applications are limited to private access; only the user who created the app can grant access.
blockers.fix: Call support at 866-289-2101 to begin the approval process for all users.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The exact error or screen other users see wasn't documented.

blockers.cause: The API key passed 10,000 requests for the day.
blockers.fix: Wait for the 00:00 UTC reset, cache and batch calls, and ask Constant Contact about higher limits during approval.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Whether higher limits can be granted isn't documented.

blockers.fix: Queue requests globally per API key and retry with backoff.

blockers.symptom: No refresh_token in the token response
blockers.cause: The authorize request didn't include the offline_access scope (or the app uses the implicit flow).
blockers.fix: Add offline_access to scope and use the authorization code or PKCE flow.

blockers.symptom: 403 when calling an endpoint with a valid token
blockers.cause: The token lacks the scope the route needs (e.g. /emails needs campaign_data).
blockers.fix: Request the right scopes and have the user re-authorize.

blockers.symptom: Token exchange fails with an expired or invalid code
blockers.fix: Exchange the code immediately on the callback.

nuances.text: Access tokens (JWTs of 1,000–1,200 characters) expire after 1,440 minutes with a 24-hour maximum; implicit-flow tokens last 8 hours. Size your token columns accordingly.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The server-flow page's sample response shows expires_in 28800, which conflicts with the 1,440-minute figure.

nuances.text: Refresh tokens are 42 characters and expire after 180 days if never used. Choose Rotating (recommended, new token on each refresh) or Long Lived when creating the app.
The 10,000/day and 4/second limits are stated for 'your API key', so a multi-tenant agent may share one budget across all connected accounts.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The docs don't say whether limits are per key or per key-and-account; we read 'your API key' literally.

nuances.text: Constant Contact doesn't publish an OIDC discovery document at its Okta-style issuer, although it returns an id_token with name and email.
Device Authorization and PKCE flows are supported for CLIs and public clients, so an agent running locally doesn't need to hold a client secret.
